readings.title: Open Data Structures: ChainedHashTable
readings.guidance: Read the overview and find/add/remove pseudocode through Section 5.1.1; stop before resizing details.
readings.supports: Explains hash-table lookup and insertion order, collision chains, and expected constant-time operations used by the complement lookup pattern.

readings.title: Pagh and Rodler: Cuckoo Hashing
readings.guidance: Read the abstract and Section 1 through the description of dictionary operations; stop before the graph analysis.
readings.supports: Places membership lookup and key-associated values in a research-grade dictionary design with constant-time lookup; its cuckoo collision scheme is an extension beyond the lesson's chained table.

readings.title: cppreference: std::unordered_map
readings.guidance: Skim the overview and the complexity table for insert/find/erase.
readings.supports: Shows a general-purpose hash map's O(1) expected lookup and insert, the operation the complement check depends on.

readings.title: Wikipedia: Hash table
readings.guidance: Skim the collision-resolution section (chaining vs. open addressing).
readings.supports: Surveys collision handling behind the map used for the seen-before check.

readings.title: Python documentation: Counter objects
readings.guidance: Jump to Counter objects and read the opening description, examples, and common patterns; stop before deque.
readings.supports: Defines frequency maps, missing-count behavior, and multiset operations that motivate count-based array reasoning.

readings.title: Misra and Gries: Finding Repeated Elements
readings.guidance: Read the statement, algorithm, and invariant on pages 1–2; stop before the program-transformation derivation.
readings.supports: Establishes the cancellation invariant behind majority-candidate algorithms and why a candidate must be verified when no majority is guaranteed.

readings.title: Wikipedia: Boyer-Moore majority vote algorithm
readings.guidance: Read the algorithm description and the correctness argument.
readings.supports: Explains why cancellation of unequal pairs finds a guaranteed majority element.

readings.title: cppreference: std::count
readings.guidance: Skim the summary and complexity.
readings.supports: Frames counting occurrences as a single linear pass, the baseline the frequency map improves on.

readings.title: University of Chicago: Anagrams and canonical form
readings.guidance: Read the problem statement through the sorted-letter representation; skip the assignment logistics and optional extensions.
readings.supports: Shows how one canonical representation turns anagram equivalence into ordinary key equality.

readings.title: Parameterized Pattern Matching — Succinctly
readings.guidance: Read the abstract and the first two pages of the introduction, focusing on the one-to-one correspondence definition.
readings.supports: Formalizes symbol matching as a bijection, supporting the lesson's need for forward and reverse maps rather than a one-way association.

readings.title: Wikipedia: Anagram
readings.guidance: Skim the definition and the algorithmic-detection section.
readings.supports: Defines the equivalence the sorted-letters key is built to detect.

readings.title: Wikipedia: Bijection
readings.guidance: Read the definition and the one-line criterion for a function to be bijective.
readings.supports: Gives the formal two-directional mapping condition the pattern-matching check must enforce.

readings.title: Python documentation: Set types
readings.guidance: Jump to Set Types and read the overview plus membership and set-operation examples; stop before mappings.
readings.supports: Distinguishes membership-only sets from structures that preserve multiplicity.

readings.title: Nivasch: Cycle Detection Using a Stack
readings.guidance: Read the author's explanation of storing visited states and the linked paper's introduction. Compare the simple stored-state detector with the proposed stack method; skip the average-case analysis.
readings.supports: Explains repeated-state cycle detection and links the author's research on a stack-based detector. The stack method is an extension to the lesson's visited-set simulation.

readings.title: James Madison CS240: Multisets
readings.guidance: Read Introduction and A Better Data Structure. Compare a set's membership answer with a multiset's count for each value; skip the programming assignment.
readings.supports: Distinguishes sets from multisets and explains storing multiplicities rather than one boolean per value.

readings.title: cppreference: std::unordered_set
readings.guidance: Skim the overview and complexity table.
readings.supports: Shows the set interface used for membership and intersection checks.

readings.title: Wikipedia: Cycle detection
readings.guidance: Read the introduction and the Floyd's tortoise-and-hare section.
readings.supports: Surveys cycle-detection strategies beyond the visited-set approach used for the digit-square sequence.

readings.title: Princeton Algorithms: Mergesort
readings.guidance: Read top-down mergesort and the merge assertion; stop before improvements and exercises.
readings.supports: Introduces divide-and-conquer merge sort, its merge invariant, and its linearithmic running time.

readings.title: Hoare: Algorithm 64 — Quicksort
readings.guidance: Read the algorithm description and partition procedure on the first two pages; focus on the moving region boundaries.
readings.supports: Provides the original partition procedure and region-boundary reasoning that underlies in-place three-way partition variants.

readings.title: cppreference: std::sort
readings.guidance: Skim the summary, complexity, and the in-place guarantee.
readings.supports: Names the comparison-sort contract the merge and partition logic must satisfy.

readings.title: Wikipedia: Dutch national flag problem
readings.guidance: Read the problem statement and the three-way partition invariant.
readings.supports: Is the exact three-region invariant Sort Colors implements in one pass.

readings.title: Goucher College: Prefix computations
readings.guidance: Read the prefix-computation definition and the first worked examples; stop before the machine-specific implementation.
readings.supports: Defines running prefix state and shows how each output summarizes all earlier inputs.

readings.title: Kogge and Stone: A Parallel Algorithm for Recurrence Equations
readings.guidance: Read pages 786–789, through the carry recurrence and parallel-prefix formulation; skip circuit-layout details.
readings.supports: Connects carry propagation to prefix recurrences and makes explicit which state must be preserved while processing digits.

readings.title: Wikipedia: Prefix sum
readings.guidance: Read the definition and the sequential-computation section.
readings.supports: Defines the running-total structure built in the array pass.

readings.title: Wikipedia: Multiplication algorithm
readings.guidance: Skim the grade-school long-multiplication section.
readings.supports: Describes the digit-by-digit, carry-resolved multiplication the digit-array accumulator implements.

readings.title: Stanford CS106A: Two-Dimensional Arrays
readings.guidance: Read slides 44–65 on two-dimensional arrays, row and column coordinates, and traversal. Focus on rectangular shape and index bounds; skip the earlier one-dimensional array exercises.
readings.supports: Explains row/column indexing, rectangular array shape, and nested traversal. These are the representation assumptions behind the lesson's matrix transformations.

readings.title: Gustavson and Walker: Algorithms for In-Place Matrix Transposition
readings.guidance: Read the abstract, introduction, and square-matrix algorithm; skip cache benchmarks and rectangular-matrix proofs.
readings.supports: Analyzes in-place matrix transposition, including the square-shape assumption and safe movement of entries.

readings.title: UIC: Two-Dimensional Coordinate Transformations
readings.guidance: Read the rotation and translation equations only. Compare rotation about the origin with re-indexing a finite grid, where a translation is also needed. Skip homogeneous-coordinate composition.
readings.supports: Gives coordinate-rotation equations. Discrete array rotation additionally shifts coordinates into valid nonnegative indices; zero marking is a separate lesson derivation.

readings.title: Wikipedia: In-place algorithm
readings.guidance: Read the definition and the auxiliary-space caveat.
readings.supports: Clarifies why writing into the same matrix still counts as O(1) auxiliary space.

readings.title: CP-Algorithms: Binary search
readings.guidance: Read the half-open interval implementation and lower-bound invariant; stop before continuous search.
readings.supports: Explains half-open binary-search boundaries and the difference between finding equality and finding an insertion boundary.

readings.title: Bentley: Writing Correct Programs
readings.guidance: Read pages 1–7 through the binary-search invariant and termination argument; skip the later testing discussion.
readings.supports: Develops binary search from a loop invariant, making boundary preservation and off-by-one correctness explicit.

readings.title: cppreference: std::lower_bound
readings.guidance: Skim the summary and the complexity note.
readings.supports: Names the first-not-less-than search this lesson's loop computes by hand.

readings.title: Wikipedia: Binary search algorithm
readings.guidance: Read the procedure section and the loop-invariant description.
readings.supports: States the shrinking-range invariant every binary search in the week relies on.

readings.title: USACO Guide: Binary search on monotonic functions
readings.guidance: Read Binary Search on Monotonic Functions and the first example; stop before the problem list.
readings.supports: Introduces searching a monotone predicate over integers and choosing the first feasible boundary.

readings.title: Zimmermann: Karatsuba Square Root
readings.guidance: Read the abstract and introduction through the SqrtRem input/output contract. Stop before the correctness proof. Compare an exact integer root and remainder with the lesson's boundary-search result.
readings.supports: Defines exact integer square root and remainder. The divide-and-conquer algorithm is a research extension, not the source of the lesson's binary-search predicate.

readings.title: Wikipedia: Monotonic function
readings.guidance: Read the definition and the one-variable examples.
readings.supports: Defines the monotone predicate property that lets binary search replace a linear scan.

readings.title: cppreference: std::upper_bound
readings.guidance: Skim the summary and the difference from lower_bound.
readings.supports: Contrasts the strict versus non-strict boundary the day's predicates must get right.

readings.title: Python documentation: Bisect
readings.guidance: Read the bisection functions and the performance notes; skip the long recipe section.
readings.supports: Defines left and right insertion points, including duplicate handling and successor queries.

readings.title: Abrahams: Binary Search with Heterogeneous Comparison
readings.guidance: Read the introduction and the lower_bound, upper_bound, and equal_range table; stop before the proposed wording.
readings.supports: Defines the standard boundary-search operations that turn duplicate equality into a lower and upper insertion range.

readings.title: UPC: Staircase Search in Sorted Matrices
readings.guidance: Read slides 18–24 on searching a row-and-column-sorted matrix. State which row or column a comparison excludes, then stop before later exercises.
readings.supports: Develops the staircase-search invariant and linear row-plus-column probe bound used for sorted-matrix elimination.

readings.title: cppreference: std::equal_range
readings.guidance: Skim the summary; note it returns both boundaries in one call.
readings.supports: Names the paired lower/upper boundary search this lesson builds from two binary searches.

readings.title: University of Washington: Arrays and sorted matrix search
readings.guidance: Read the row-major indexing and sorted-matrix search slides; skip Java array covariance.
readings.supports: Contrasts row-major flattening with row-and-column order and derives the staircase elimination step.

readings.title: Dijkstra: The Saddleback Search
readings.guidance: Read pages 1–4 through the invariant and guarded-command derivation; skip the final generalization.
readings.supports: Derives the sorted-grid staircase search from an invariant and proves why each comparison removes a row or column.

readings.title: Princeton: Finding the Minimum of a Rotated Sorted Array
readings.guidance: Read the class description and findMinimumIndex method. Track the comparison with the right endpoint and explain why the midpoint remains a candidate on one branch.
readings.supports: Provides the distinct-key rotated-minimum algorithm and its midpoint/right-end boundary rule.

readings.title: cppreference: std::rotate
readings.guidance: Skim the summary and the in-place rotation guarantee.
readings.supports: Frames a rotated sorted array as a cyclic shift, the structure the search must exploit.

readings.title: MIT 6.006: Peak finding
readings.guidance: Read the lecture summary and view the 1D peak-finding portion through the divide-and-conquer algorithm.
readings.supports: Introduces local peaks and explains why the neighboring slope identifies a half that still contains a peak.

readings.title: MIT 6.006 Recitation 2: Peak Finding
readings.guidance: Read the 1D peak definition, algorithm, and correctness argument; skip the 2D extension.
readings.supports: Provides a compact proof of logarithmic peak finding by preserving existence in the retained interval.

readings.title: Zhang: New Upper and Lower Bounds for Randomized and Quantum Local Search
readings.guidance: Read the abstract and the opening definition of local search. View array positions as a path graph whose vertex values are the array entries; stop before the quantum bounds.
readings.supports: Formalizes finding a local optimum of a function on a graph, a research extension of the lesson's local-peak objective from an array path to broader graph families.

readings.title: MIT 6.006: Rotated-Array Binary Search
readings.guidance: Read pages 5–6 on rotated arrays and which ordered half to retain. Stop after the elimination argument. Then consider why equal endpoints make that decision ambiguous.
readings.supports: Explains binary search on a rotated sorted array. The lesson adds the duplicate-heavy worst-case caveat.

readings.title: Topcoder: Binary Search
readings.guidance: Read the monotonic-function and binary-search-the-answer sections; skip the contest-problem catalog.
readings.supports: Shows how to turn an optimization problem into a monotone feasibility question over candidate answers.

readings.title: Agarwal, Sharir, and Toledo: Applications of Parametric Searching
readings.guidance: Read the abstract and introduction through the parametric-search outline; skip the geometry-specific algorithms.
readings.supports: Formalizes optimization via repeated decision tests and separates feasibility from the search that finds the optimum.

readings.title: Wikipedia: Bisection method
readings.guidance: Read the algorithm section for root-finding by halving an interval.
readings.supports: Is the continuous-domain ancestor of binary-searching the answer over a feasibility predicate.

readings.title: cppreference: std::partition_point
readings.guidance: Skim the summary; note the precondition that the range is already partitioned.
readings.supports: Matches exactly the search-the-answer pattern: find the boundary of a monotone true/false predicate.

readings.title: University of Toronto: Binary search
readings.guidance: Read the illustrated trace and its loop invariant through the not-found example.
readings.supports: Reviews the ordered-boundary invariant used by all three lesson problems.

readings.title: de Berg and Thite: Cache-Oblivious Selection in Sorted X+Y Matrices
readings.guidance: Read the abstract and Section 1 through the definition of the sorted X+Y matrix; skip the cache analysis.
readings.supports: Studies rank and selection over pairwise combinations of sorted arrays, the research setting closest to the lesson's count-pairs boundary search.

readings.title: Princeton Competitive Programming: Binary Search on the Answer
readings.guidance: Read the Problem C binary-search-the-answer discussion. Identify the candidate answer, feasibility predicate, and search bounds; skip the other problems.
readings.supports: Explains searching a monotone feasibility predicate and choosing answer bounds, which the lesson applies to several different counting checks.

readings.title: Wikipedia: Interpolation search
readings.guidance: Skim the idea section contrasting it with plain binary search.
readings.supports: Reviews a related search strategy as contrast before applying plain binary search to paired arrays.

readings.title: USACO Guide: Two pointers
readings.guidance: Read the opposite-end two-pointer explanation and Sum of Two Values trace; stop before the problem list.
readings.supports: Explains why sorted order makes it safe to discard one endpoint after each comparison.

readings.title: Berenbrink et al.: Palindrome Recognition in the Streaming Model
readings.guidance: Read the abstract and Section 1 through the definitions of the palindrome and longest-palindromic-substring problems; stop before the algorithmic results.
readings.supports: Defines palindrome recognition and its center-based string model in the algorithms literature; the lesson's whole-string normalization and two-pointer check are a simpler special case.

readings.title: cppreference: std::equal
readings.guidance: Skim the summary.
readings.supports: Is the range-equality check two converging pointers perform one step at a time for a palindrome.

readings.title: cppreference: std::reverse
readings.guidance: Skim the summary and the in-place, linear-time guarantee.
readings.supports: Is the two-pointer swap-from-the-ends pattern applied to reversing a sequence.

readings.title: Open Data Structures: Array-based lists
readings.guidance: Read the ArrayStack representation and get/set/add/remove overview; focus on how a valid prefix is stored.
readings.supports: Provides the array-prefix model needed to reason about separate read and write indices during in-place compaction.

readings.title: Katajainen and Pasanen: Stable Minimum Space Partitioning
readings.guidance: Read the abstract, introduction, and definition of stability; skip the packed-word implementation.
readings.supports: Defines stable in-place partitioning and makes clear why preserving the relative order of retained values is a separate requirement.

readings.title: cppreference: std::remove
readings.guidance: Skim the summary and the erase-remove idiom note.
readings.supports: Shows the same read/write pointer pattern used to compact an array in place.

readings.title: cppreference: std::unique
readings.guidance: Skim the summary; note it removes consecutive duplicates in place.
readings.supports: Is the standard-library operation that matches Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array exactly.

readings.title: Princeton Algorithms: Analysis of algorithms
readings.guidance: Read the 3-sum discussion and doubling observations; stop before the memory model.
readings.supports: Introduces 3SUM, the cubic baseline, and why algorithm structure matters to running time.

readings.title: Grønlund and Pettie: Threesomes, Degenerates, and Love Triangles
readings.guidance: Read the abstract and first two pages of the introduction; stop before the decision-tree machinery.
readings.supports: Gives the formal 3SUM problem and its complexity context; the lesson uses the practical sorted two-pointer solution rather than the paper's advanced bounds.

readings.title: Dartmouth CS31: Two-Pointer Technique
readings.guidance: Read pages 1–3 on ordered pair search and the 3SUM extension. State why moving an endpoint discards only impossible pairs.
readings.supports: Explains elimination of sorted pair candidates and extending the scan to triples. The container-height argument in the lesson is a separate application.

readings.title: Wikipedia: 3SUM
readings.guidance: Read the problem statement and the sort-then-two-pointer algorithm section.
readings.supports: Is the exact problem and canonical O(n^2) approach this lesson's core problems implement.

readings.title: GNU Scientific Library: Moving-window statistics
readings.guidance: Read the introduction and fixed-endpoint moving-sum examples; skip C API details.
readings.supports: Introduces fixed-width windows and incremental aggregate updates as one value enters and one leaves.

readings.title: Datar et al.: Maintaining Stream Statistics over Sliding Windows
readings.guidance: Read the abstract and Sections 1–2 through the exact-window model; skip exponential histograms.
readings.supports: Formalizes window boundaries and expiring observations, which underlie fixed-window sum and count invariants.

readings.title: Wikipedia: Moving average
readings.guidance: Skim the simple moving average section.
readings.supports: Is a fixed-size window statistic recomputed incrementally, the same shape as this lesson's problems.

readings.title: cppreference: std::accumulate
readings.guidance: Skim the summary.
readings.supports: Names the running-sum reduction the window's incremental update avoids recomputing.

readings.title: OI Wiki: Two pointers
readings.guidance: Read the same-direction pointer pattern and its linear-time argument; skip unrelated practice problems.
readings.supports: Shows why a left boundary that only moves forward yields linear work in variable-window algorithms.

readings.title: Braverman and Ostrovsky: Smooth Histograms for Sliding Windows
readings.guidance: Read the abstract and Section 1 through the sliding-window model; skip the approximation proofs.
readings.supports: Defines streaming sliding windows and explains why expiring old state is difficult; its approximate model differs from the lesson's exact in-memory windows.

readings.title: Wikipedia: String (computer science)
readings.guidance: Skim the operations section covering substrings.
readings.supports: Defines the substring unit a variable window expands and shrinks over while tracking validity.

readings.title: cppreference: std::map
readings.guidance: Skim the overview; note the ordered, logarithmic-time operations.
readings.supports: Contrasts an ordered map's O(log n) operations with the O(1) expected operations the window's frequency map relies on.

readings.title: USACO Guide: Prefix sums
readings.guidance: Read the prefix-sum definition and subarray-sum derivation; stop before two-dimensional sums.
readings.supports: Derives a subarray sum as the difference of two prefixes, the identity used by the target-sum frequency map.

readings.title: Blelloch: Prefix Sums and Their Applications
readings.guidance: Read Sections 1.1–1.3 through the scan definition and examples; skip the parallel implementation details.
readings.supports: Defines scan as a general operation and shows how prefix state represents all earlier elements; the lesson adds a frequency map and the empty-prefix seed.

readings.title: Wikipedia: Associative array
readings.guidance: Skim the definition and operations.
readings.supports: Generalises the frequency map used to count prefix sums seen so far.

readings.title: cppreference: std::partial_sum
readings.guidance: Skim the summary.
readings.supports: Is the standard-library operation that computes exactly the prefix-sum array this lesson builds by hand.

readings.title: Carnegie Mellon: Scan algorithms
readings.guidance: Read the scan definition and applications list, then inspect the prefix-products example; skip implementation links.
readings.supports: Shows that prefix aggregation works for associative operations beyond addition, including products.

readings.title: Chatterjee, Blelloch, and Zagha: Scan Primitives for Vector Computers
readings.guidance: Read the abstract and Sections 1–2 through the scan primitives; skip vector-machine performance results.
readings.supports: Formalizes inclusive and exclusive scans, supporting prefix/suffix product construction without division.

readings.title: Go specification: Arithmetic operators
readings.guidance: Read integer quotient and remainder semantics, including the sign rule; stop before floating-point operators.
readings.supports: Documents signed remainder behavior, explaining why modulo keys must be normalized before frequency-map lookup.

readings.title: Wikipedia: Modular arithmetic
readings.guidance: Read the definition and the congruence notation.
readings.supports: Explains the remainder classes a prefix-product-mod-k state tracks.

readings.title: Open Data Structures: Singly-linked lists
readings.guidance: Read the representation and add/remove pointer updates; stop before the queue analysis.
readings.supports: Introduces link rewiring and shows why the old next pointer must be saved before changing a node.

readings.title: Reynolds: Separation Logic — A Logic for Shared Mutable Data Structures
readings.guidance: Read the abstract and pages 1–2 through the in-place list-reversal example. Stop before the programming-language semantics. Track the saved next pointer and disjoint list segments.
readings.supports: Models disjoint linked segments and local pointer mutation, the reasoning needed for reversal and merge without losing nodes.

readings.title: Wikipedia: Linked list
readings.guidance: Skim the singly linked list section and the reversal description.
readings.supports: Reviews the pointer-rewiring model this lesson's reversal and merge operations rely on.

readings.title: cppreference: std::forward_list
readings.guidance: Skim the overview.
readings.supports: Shows a standard-library singly linked list interface for comparison with the hand-rolled node struct.

readings.title: Cornell: Linked lists
readings.guidance: Read the node-identity, traversal, and pointer-diagram sections; stop before Java iterator details.
readings.supports: Establishes reference identity and traversal state, which distinguish intersecting nodes from merely equal values.

readings.title: Sedgewick, Szymanski, and Yao: The Complexity of Finding Cycles in Periodic Functions
readings.guidance: Read pages 376–379 through Floyd's algorithm and its cost analysis; skip the later lower-bound proofs.
readings.supports: States and analyzes the two-speed tortoise-and-hare method used for constant-space linked-list cycle detection.

readings.title: Wikipedia: Pointer (computer programming)
readings.guidance: Skim the definition and the traversal example.
readings.supports: Reviews the reference-following model behind advancing a fast pointer twice for every one step of a slow pointer.

readings.title: cppreference: std::advance
readings.guidance: Skim the summary.
readings.supports: Names the generic operation of moving a pointer forward by a fixed number of steps, done at two different rates here.

readings.title: Princeton: Verifying linked-list reversal
readings.guidance: Read the reversal code and diagram plus the informal invariant; skip the Coq proof commands.
readings.supports: Makes the reversed-prefix and unprocessed-suffix invariant visible during in-place list reversal.

readings.title: Myreen: Separation Logic Adapted for Proofs by Rewriting
readings.guidance: Read the abstract and linked-list reversal example in Sections 1–2; skip the proof-engine implementation.
readings.supports: Uses list reversal to show how ownership and segment invariants prevent pointer loss, relevant when reversing and restoring a palindrome half.

readings.title: Competitive Programmer's Handbook: Floyd's algorithm
readings.guidance: Read pages 104–105 on cycle detection and the cycle-entry argument only.
readings.supports: Explains the phase-reset step that locates a cycle entry after fast and slow pointers first meet.

readings.title: Wikipedia: Palindrome
readings.guidance: Skim the definition.
readings.supports: Defines the symmetry property the half-list comparison problem checks.

readings.title: Cornell CS410: Linked-list implementation
readings.guidance: Read the sentinel-node and insertion/deletion diagrams; skip the C++ template details.
readings.supports: Shows how sentinel nodes remove head special cases and how pointer rewiring preserves the rest of a list.

readings.title: Salowe and Steiger: Stable Unmerging in Linear Time and Constant Space
readings.guidance: Read the abstract and introductory definition of stable unmerging; stop before the block-rotation construction.
readings.supports: Formalizes stable separation while preserving relative order, matching the lesson's tail-based linked-list partition invariant.

readings.title: Wikipedia: Sentinel value
readings.guidance: Read the definition and the dummy-node use case.
readings.supports: Is the general technique behind the dummy head node this lesson uses to avoid special-casing the list head.

readings.title: Wikipedia: Doubly linked list
readings.guidance: Skim the definition and the insertion/removal diagrams.
readings.supports: Shows the two-pointer node structure a stable partition must keep consistent while splicing nodes out.

readings.title: Princeton Algorithms: Stacks
readings.guidance: Read the stack API, delimiter matching, and Dijkstra two-stack evaluation; stop before resizing-array analysis.
readings.supports: Introduces LIFO state for delimiter validation and expression evaluation, including operand order.

readings.title: Dijkstra: ALGOL 60 Translation
readings.guidance: Open the report and read pages 8–11 on algebraic expressions and the accumulator stack; skip object-machine details.
readings.supports: Provides the historical operator-stack technique behind stack-based expression parsing and postfix evaluation.

readings.title: Wikipedia: Stack (abstract data type)
readings.guidance: Skim the operations list and the LIFO property.
readings.supports: States the last-in-first-out contract the day's stack-based problems depend on.

readings.title: cppreference: std::stack
readings.guidance: Skim the overview.
readings.supports: Shows a standard-library stack adaptor for comparison with a hand-rolled slice-backed stack.

readings.title: Open Data Structures: DualArrayDeque
readings.guidance: Read the two-array representation and rebalancing argument; focus on how reversing one side restores order.
readings.supports: Shows how two LIFO-oriented halves can represent FIFO order and why occasional bulk transfer can be amortized.

readings.title: Hood and Melville: Real-Time Queue Operations in Pure LISP
readings.guidance: Read the abstract and Sections 1–2 through the two-list queue; skip the incremental scheduling construction.
readings.supports: Develops queues from front and rear lists and explains the reversal cost that amortized two-stack queues distribute across operations.

readings.title: cppreference: std::queue
readings.guidance: Skim the overview and the underlying-container note.
readings.supports: Shows a standard queue adaptor, the interface being rebuilt on top of a different structure.

readings.title: Go: container/list package
readings.guidance: Skim the package overview.
readings.supports: Shows a standard-library doubly linked list, a different underlying structure than the array-backed queue built here.

readings.title: Jeff Erickson: Recursion
readings.guidance: Read the opening recurrence examples and fast exponentiation section; stop before exhaustive search.
readings.supports: Explains recursive contracts, base cases, decreasing measures, and exponentiation by squaring.

readings.title: Michie: ‘Memo’ Functions and Machine Learning
readings.guidance: Read the full two-page note, focusing on the memoized Fibonacci example and stored argument-result pairs.
readings.supports: Introduces memoization through Fibonacci and shows how caching changes repeated recursion into one computation per distinct state.

readings.title: Wikipedia: Recursion (computer science)
readings.guidance: Read the base case and recursive case section.
readings.supports: States the base-case-plus-smaller-subproblem contract every recursive function in the day must satisfy.

readings.title: Wikipedia: Recursion
readings.guidance: Skim the definition, outside the computer-science-specific section.
readings.supports: Gives the general self-reference concept before narrowing to recursive functions.
